what_its_for: Lenacapavir is a medicine used to treat HIV-1 infection in adults. It is used together with other HIV medicines when other treatments have stopped working or are no longer suitable for you. It works by blocking a part of the HIV virus called the capsid, which stops the virus from multiplying in your body.
how_to_take: Lenacapavir comes in two forms: tablets taken by mouth and an injection given under the skin (subcutaneous injection). When you first start this medicine, your doctor will give you tablets to take for a few days, and then you will receive injections every 6 months (twice a year). The injections are given by your doctor or nurse at a clinic — you should NOT try to inject yourself at home. Take the tablets with or without food. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or split them.
dosing: The usual starting schedule is: Days 1 and 2 — take two 300 mg tablets (600 mg total) by mouth on Day 1, and one 300 mg tablet by mouth on Day 2. Then on Day 8 — you receive two injections of 1.5 mL each (927 mg total) under the skin at your clinic. After that, you return to the clinic every 6 months (approximately every 26 weeks) for your maintenance injection (two 1.5 mL injections). Always follow your doctor's exact instructions, as your schedule may be slightly different.
missed_dose: If you miss your scheduled injection appointment, contact your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to reschedule. Do not skip or delay your injection without talking to your healthcare team first. If you miss one of the starting tablets, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If a full day has passed, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule — do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Tablets: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them in the original container, away from moisture and heat. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep out of reach of children. Injections: The injections are stored and handled by your healthcare provider at the clinic — you do not need to store them at home.
what_to_avoid: Do not take lenacapavir with certain other medicines without telling your doctor, as some drugs can interfere with how lenacapavir works or cause harmful side effects. These include some seizure medicines (like carbamazepine, phenytoin), some antibiotics (like rifampin), and some herbal supplements (like St. John's Wort). Always tell every doctor, dentist, and pharmacist that you are taking lenacapavir before starting any new medicine, vitamin, or supplement. Do not stop taking your other HIV medicines unless your doctor tells you to. Lenacapavir does not prevent transmission of HIV to others — continue to use safer sex practices such as condoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: pain, redness, swelling, hardness, or a lump at the injection site that does not go away or gets worse; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; unusual tiredness, nausea, or vomiting; any new or worsening symptoms after starting treatment; or if you become pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
when_it_works: Lenacapavir starts working soon after you begin treatment, but it may take several weeks before your lab tests (viral load and CD4 count) show improvement. It is very important that you keep all of your clinic appointments for your injection every 6 months to keep the medicine working. Missing injections can allow the HIV virus to start multiplying again and may cause the medicine to stop working over time.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is recommended that people with HIV do not breastfeed to avoid passing the virus to their baby. The safety of lenacapavir during pregnancy is not fully known — talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as this may affect how the medicine works in your body. Children: Lenacapavir is currently approved only for adults (18 years and older). Older adults: No dose adjustment is generally needed for older adults, but your doctor will monitor you closely.
